ordered_arithmetic: Load h, previous FFN output o, prior scale2 g, and norm1 weight w from FP16 and convert to FP32.
raw = IEEE-RN FP32 fma(o,g,h); this is one fused multiply-add before any FP16 residual rounding.

Compute sum_sq from raw FP32 values before residual rounding. Each lane sums its 8-value segment with the explicit alternating mul.rn/fma.rn/add.rn sequence, then the tested 8-warp blocked-layout reduction tree reduces partials.
Cast raw to FP16, store the residual into H, and reload/cast that stored FP16 residual to FP32 for normalization. Therefore statistics use raw while normalized numerator uses rounded residual.
inv_rms = libdevice.rsqrt(sum_sq / 2048 + 1e-5); multiply residual_fp32 by inv_rms, then by w_fp32, and cast normalized activation to FP16.

CK rowwise activation contract: per-row FP32 amax; S=max(amax*(1/127),1e-30) in FP32; denominator is FP16(S) widened to FP32; divide RN, cast quotient to FP16 then FP32, libdevice.nearbyint under the tested CUDA rounding mode, NaN to -128, clamp [-128,127], store Q as INT8.

Feed Q/S once to the existing public-CK-compatible prequantized INT8 GEMM with unchanged int8 qweight, FP32 weight scales and FP16 bias; compare the restored [4,1797,6144] output against public CK int8_linear on the same normalized activation.

register_and_lane_mapping.derivation: tid.x maps to col_base = 4*(tid.x & 511); each CTA covers one 2048-wide row with 512 threads. lane=tid&31, warp=tid>>5.
The packed loads/conversions construct raw pair [raw(4*t+0),raw(4*t+1)] in rd21 and [raw(4*t+2),raw(4*t+3)] in rd26. fma.rn.f32x2 performs the residual FMA independently per packed component.
mul.f32x2 produces the four independent raw squares before H is stored as FP16; PTX default floating rounding is RN. No square is taken from the rounded residual.

ptx_trace.meaning: Extract square(x1) to r45 and put it in rd28 low; fma.rn.f32x2 with rd21 yields low = fma.rn(x0,x0,square(x1)), then fma.rn.f32x2 with rd26 yields low = fma.rn(x2,x2,a).
Extract square(x3) to r47, place it in rd31 low; add.f32x2 yields low = square(x3)+b, and mov {r49,_},rd32 extracts that low result as the lane partial.

lane_local_scalar_recipe.packed_dead_lane_note: r46 (and r48) are the high words in rd28/rd31. They only feed the high independent f32x2 lane; the final scalar extracts the low word. PTX does not establish r46/r48 == 0, and zero is unnecessary for the low-lane recipe.
lane_local_scalar_recipe.confidence: High for the low scalar dependency and order; derived from exact low/high word extraction, PTX fma/mul/add instructions, and final low-word extraction.

warp_tree.operation: For each warp lane l, begin v_l=p_l; for offsets d=(16,8,4,2,1), set v_l=add.rn(v_l, shuffle_xor(v,d)). Each stage uses the prior-stage value from both lanes; warp subtotal is lane 0 after d=1.
warp_tree.warp_lane_coverage: 32 lane partials, each covering 4 contiguous columns; one warp covers 128 columns.

cta_crosswarp_tree.operation: Lane 0 of each of 16 warps writes one subtotal to shared[warp_id]. After barrier, CTA threads 0..15 load those 16 values; warp-0 XOR/add stages d=(8,4,2,1) reduce them. Thread 0 writes the result to shared; after the second barrier, all threads load the scalar row sum.
cta_crosswarp_tree.cta_coverage: 16 warps x 32 lanes x 4 values = 2048 columns for XBLOCK=1.

warp_and_cta_tree.complete_scalar_spec: sum_sq = the ordered CTA tree over p_t: per-thread four-value recipe above; per-warp XOR/add tree offsets 16,8,4,2,1; then 16-warp shared/XOR/add tree offsets 8,4,2,1.

w8_local_tree.recipe: For each lane raw0..raw7: s1=mul(raw1,raw1); a=fma(raw0,raw0,s1); a=fma(raw2,raw2,a); a=add(mul(raw3,raw3),a); a=fma(raw4,raw4,a); a=add(mul(raw5,raw5),a); a=fma(raw6,raw6,a); partial8=add(mul(raw7,raw7),a).

comparison_to_validated_w8_tree.w8_cta_tree: reference_7188.ptx:393-428 stores two row subtotals per warp and reduces 8 warp values per row with XOR offsets 4,2,1.
comparison_to_validated_w8_tree.difference: W16 lane subtotal is exactly the first-four-value prefix tree. W16 uses 4 values x 512 threads x 16 warps per row; W8 uses 8 values x 256 threads x 8 warps per row. Their per-lane grouping and CTA reduction extent/order differ, so no W8/W16 equivalence is implied.
